topic: The 'Social Loafing' effect in remote collaborative work environments
subject: society

facts.claim: Perceived playfulness, perceived ease of use, and xenophobia are linked to an individual's social loafing in a virtual team.
facts.quote: The results showed that the perceived playfulness, perceived ease of use, and xenophobia were able to predict an individual’s social loafing, but the perceived usefulness is not able to predict it.

facts.claim: In an online experiment with N = 102, participants showed social loafing tendencies in virtual collaboration with virtual assistants and tended to cede responsibility to the virtual assistant.
facts.quote: The results indicate SL tendencies in virtual collaboration with VAs and that participants tend to cede responsibility to the VA.

facts.claim: Factors contributing to social loafing in online learning include group size, internet connectivity issues, digital distractions, and types of leaders.
facts.quote: The Factors of Online Learning that Contribute to Social Loafing has four (4) emergent themes that were classified: Group size, Internet Connectivity issue, Digital distractions, and Types of Leaders

facts.claim: Group size is linked to social loafing behaviors.
facts.quote: Group size was found to be positively correlated with social loafing behaviors, but no significant relationship was found with task visibility.

facts.claim: In a study of university language learners, some students did not do their share of the work and engaged in social loafing and free riding.
facts.quote: While most students contributed to content and editing of their wiki page as required, some students did not do their share of the work and engaged in social loafing and free riding.

research.angle: Social loafing in remote work is linked to larger group sizes and the presence of virtual assistants, but it is also influenced by psychological factors like perceived playfulness and digital distractions.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that social loafing occurs in virtual and online environments, often correlating with larger group sizes and the delegation of responsibility to technology.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide a definitive causal link between the difficulty of monitoring individual contributions and the increase in social loafing.
